mn_minnesota_strip.blurb: The Minnesota Strip is the tallest cliff line within Interstate State Park at Taylors Falls, with faces roughly 70 to 90 feet high. Nineteen mostly traditional climbs run from easy fifth class to a few hard ones in the low 5.13 range, though the bulk sit between 5.5 and 5.11 and are protected with hand-placed gear. One climb is top-rope only. The basalt is solid and the wall catches enough sun to make early spring and late autumn days in the 40s pleasant. It is a classic for climbers learning to lead on natural protection, but expect tourists and other parties around it.

mn_pit_aka_arm_pit_the.blurb: The Pit sits just below the walkway near the river in Interstate State Park at Taylors Falls, among the first boulders you meet on arrival. Most of its nineteen climbs are boulder problems, from very easy up to V5 with one much harder line, and a few trad and top-rope routes join them. The basalt is slick and polished, so expect slopers, thin crimps and balance-heavy moves rather than big holds. Its easy problems make it a sensible warm-up spot for the neighbouring walls. Summer brings mosquitoes and bees, and the park's boulders can be climbed through much of the year.

mn_sizzlefoot_wall.blurb: At Taylors Falls in Interstate State Park, Sizzlefoot Wall is among the most prominent bits of rock, below the ramp that descends to the river. The face is long, about fifty feet, with a few boulders along its base. Eighteen boulder problems cover a wide range: a handful of easy ones for beginners, a solid middle group around V3 and V4, and a few much harder lines up to V10. Several tough top-ropes share the wall. The basalt here is polished, so slopers and poor feet are the norm. Summer means mosquitoes and bees.

_expect.name: Boonyards aka The B2 Pit, The

mn_boonyards_aka_the_b2_pit_the.blurb: The Boonyards, also called the B2 Pit, is a tucked-away pothole in Interstate State Park at Taylors Falls that offers a quieter corner away from the park's visitors. It holds sixteen boulder problems, mostly V3 to V7 with a few easier and two or three much harder, up to V11. A short crack line or two and one of the best-regarded problems on the Minnesota side are here. The floor turns muddy in spring and after rain, so a tarp under the pad helps. Rock is polished basalt, and summer brings mosquitoes and bees.

mn_quarry_park_st_cloud.blurb: Quarry Park and Nature Preserve is a county park southwest of St. Cloud built around old red granite quarries. Climbing is a small part of it: a roped wall in one quarry with beginner-to-advanced routes of about 20 to 30 feet, plus a separate bouldering area close to another quarry. Nineteen climbs are known, split among sport routes, boulder problems, and a few trad and top-rope lines. Boulder grades are mostly easy, while the roped routes range from moderate to a couple of hard ones. The park is open all year and is also popular for swimming and hiking, so expect company in summer.

mn_diagonals_wall_2.blurb: Diagonals Wall is a south-facing sport wall in Robinson Park, an old quarry on the edge of Sandstone. Its eighteen routes are mostly bolted, with a few trad lines, and run from easy up to the low 5.11s, with the biggest group at 5.10. Many climbs on the left and middle can be top-roped from above, while the right side needs a traverse to set up. Several ledges mean leaders should watch for ankle-twisting falls. The sun makes it a good choice on mild winter days, and it can be climbed through most of the year; summer calls for early starts and bug spray.

mn_cyclops_area.blurb: The Cyclops Area is a south-facing wall on Barn Bluff in Red Wing, left of the Winter Wall. It holds seventeen climbs, nearly all of them bolted sport routes, with one top-rope and one trad line. Grades start around 5.8 and are concentrated in the 5.10 to 5.12 range, so this is more a place for intermediate and strong climbers than for beginners. A large hole in the cliff is the landmark, and a prominent crack sits beside it. The dolomite is reported to be loose in places, with rockfall after a past controlled burn, so a helmet is wise.

mn_section_13.blurb: Section 13 is a north-facing anorthosite bluff of about 60 feet above the Superior Hiking Trail on the North Shore, near Finland. Seventeen routes, a mix of trad and top-rope lines, run from 5.6 to 5.11, with the largest group at 5.11 and the rest spread through the 5.8 to 5.10 range. The rock is cleaner than on the nearby lakeside cliffs. Routes are reached by going to the top first and rappelling down, so bring gear for anchors. It tends to be quieter than the busier lakeshore cliffs, and the clifftop views over the valleys are a bonus.
mn_section_13.parking_note: Leave the car at the Superior Hiking Trail lot on Lake County Road 6, a little over two miles inland from Highway 61 near mile marker 65, on the right-hand side.
